questionText: How many Great Pyramids stand on the Giza Plateau?
hint: They are named after three pharaohs.

questionText: Which pharaoh is credited with building the Great Pyramid?
hint: He was the second ruler of the 4th dynasty.

questionText: In which direction does the Nile River flow?
hint: It runs toward the Mediterranean Sea.

questionText: What was papyrus primarily used for in Ancient Egypt?
hint: The English word "paper" is derived from it.

questionText: Which famous pharaoh tomb was discovered almost completely intact in 1922 by Howard Carter?
hint: He became king at a very young age.

questionText: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
hint: It is named after the Roman god of war.

questionText: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
hint: It is famous for its Great Red Spot.

questionText: What is a stellar nursery primarily composed of?
hint: New stars are born inside these giant clouds.

questionText: What is the boundary around a black hole called?
hint: Nothing, not even light, can escape from inside it.

questionText: What radiation did Stephen Hawking show black holes emit?
hint: It is named after the physicist himself.

questionText: What is the largest coral reef system in the world?
hint: It lies off the coast of Australia.

questionText: What type of tiny animal builds coral reefs?
hint: Small creatures with stinging tentacles.

questionText: Which is the largest animal ever known to have lived?
hint: A whale that can grow over 30 meters long.

questionText: Which is the largest fish in the ocean?
hint: A gentle giant covered in pale spots.

questionText: What is the deepest part of the world's oceans?
hint: It lies in the western Pacific Ocean.

questionText: Which ocean zone receives no sunlight at all?
hint: It is also called the bathypelagic zone.

questionText: What does the word "dinosaur" mean?
hint: It comes from Greek words meaning "terrible lizard".

questionText: Which era is known as the Age of Dinosaurs?
hint: It includes the Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous periods.

questionText: Which meat-eating dinosaur is famous for its tiny arms?
hint: Its name means "tyrant lizard king".

questionText: Which dinosaur was a long-necked plant-eater?
hint: One of the largest land animals ever.

questionText: What is the most widely accepted cause of the dinosaur extinction?
hint: A giant space rock struck near Mexico 66 million years ago.

questionText: Which period marks the end of the dinosaurs?
hint: It ends with the K-Pg extinction event.

questionText: What was the tall central tower of a castle called?
hint: The strongest and most protected part of the castle.

questionText: What is the water-filled ditch around a castle called?
hint: It made it harder for attackers to reach the walls.

questionText: What was the ceremony called in which a man became a knight?
hint: A sword was tapped on each shoulder.

questionText: What did knights wear for protection in battle?
hint: Armor made of interlocking metal rings.

questionText: What large gathering brought traders and entertainers to medieval towns?
hint: A regular market where people bought and sold goods.

questionText: What was the open space in the center of a medieval town called?
hint: The heart of the town where trading took place.

questionText: What is the leafy top layer of the rainforest called?
hint: The roof formed by the branches of tall trees.

questionText: Which rainforest layer receives the most sunlight?
hint: The tallest trees that rise above the canopy.

questionText: What is the largest rainforest in the world?
hint: It spans across South America.

questionText: Which bird is famous for its large, colorful beak?
hint: Its beak can be bigger than its head.

questionText: What should you do if you get lost in a rainforest?
optionB: Stay put and signal for help
hint: Rescuers find moving people harder to locate.

questionText: Which plant can provide a safe drink of water in a rainforest?
hint: Its hollow stems can hold clean water.

questionText: What covers most of the Earth's surface?
hint: About 71 percent of Earth is covered by water.

questionText: How many major oceans are there?
hint: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, and Arctic.

questionText: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
hint: It covers more than a third of the planet.

questionText: What color is a healthy coral reef?
hint: Healthy corals are home to colorful algae.

questionText: What do coral reefs provide for fish?
hint: Reefs are home to about a quarter of sea life.

questionText: Which ocean animal has eight arms?
hint: Octopus means eight-footed.

questionText: Which of these ocean animals is a fish?
hint: Sharks breathe with gills like all fish.

questionText: What does a whale use to breathe air?
hint: Whales must rise to the surface to breathe.

questionText: What is a group of fish swimming together called?
hint: Fish swim in schools to stay safe.

questionText: Which beach animal has a hard shell and pincers?
hint: Crabs scuttle sideways on sandy beaches.

questionText: What usually causes ocean waves?
hint: Wind pushes the water into waves.

questionText: Which sea creature can glow in the dark?
hint: Many jellyfish produce their own light.

questionText: What is a baby whale called?
hint: A young whale is known as a calf.

questionText: Which fish hides among sea anemones?
hint: Clownfish are safe from the anemone sting.

questionText: What do sea turtles mostly eat?
hint: Most sea turtles graze on sea plants or jellyfish.

questionText: What is the highest point of a wave called?
hint: The crest is the top of a wave.

questionText: What kind of animal is a starfish?
hint: Starfish are related to sea urchins.

questionText: What do we call animals that live only in the sea?
hint: Marine means living in the ocean.

questionText: Which of these animals lives on a coral reef?
hint: Pufferfish live among coral reefs.

questionText: What is the sandy area along the ocean called?
hint: Beaches are made of sand and pebbles.

questionText: Which fish has a long sword-like snout?
hint: The swordfish uses its snout to stun prey.

questionText: What do fish use to swim through water?
hint: Fins steer and push fish forward.

questionText: What is the study of the ocean called?
hint: Oceanography is the study of oceans.

questionText: Which animal travels thousands of miles across the ocean?
hint: Whales migrate to feed and breed.

questionText: What is the white foam you see at the beach?
hint: Sea foam forms from stirred-up ocean matter.

questionText: Which sea creature stings with its tentacles?
hint: Jellyfish stun prey with stinging cells.

questionText: What do we call the rising and falling of the sea?
hint: Tides are caused by the Moon's gravity.

questionText: Which of these is NOT an ocean animal?
hint: Eagles build nests high in the sky.

questionText: What is the largest animal ever known to have lived?
hint: Blue whales reach over 30 meters long.

questionText: How much can a blue whale weigh?
hint: The blue whale can weigh as much as 200 tons.

questionText: What is the fastest fish in the ocean?
hint: Sailfish can swim over 100 km per hour.

questionText: Which land animal is the closest living relative of whales?
hint: DNA shows whales are related to hippos.

questionText: How do baleen whales feed?
hint: Baleen plates filter food from the water.

questionText: What do orcas hunt?
hint: Orcas are top ocean predators.

questionText: Which whale is famous for singing long songs?
hint: Male humpbacks sing the longest songs.

questionText: What is the largest shark in the ocean?
hint: Whale sharks can reach 18 meters.

questionText: What special sense do sharks use to find prey?
hint: They sense the electric fields of other animals.

questionText: How long can a sperm whale stay underwater?
hint: Sperm whales make long, deep dives.

questionText: Which deep-sea giant has the largest eyes?
hint: Giant squid eyes can be 25 centimeters wide.

questionText: What do manatees eat?
hint: Manatees graze peacefully on sea plants.

questionText: Which whale actually belongs to the dolphin family?
hint: Orcas are the largest dolphins.

questionText: What is the largest animal without a backbone?
hint: Giant squid are the largest invertebrates.

questionText: How do whales communicate across long distances?
hint: Whale songs travel far underwater.

questionText: What is the top predator of the Arctic Ocean?
hint: Polar bears hunt seals on the ice.

questionText: What do manta rays filter from the water?
hint: Manta rays feed on tiny plankton.

questionText: Which whale has a long spiraled tusk?
hint: The narwhal's tusk is an overgrown tooth.

questionText: How deep is the Mariana Trench?
hint: It is nearly 11 kilometers deep.

questionText: What is the deepest known point on Earth called?
hint: Challenger Deep sits in the Mariana Trench.

questionText: What is the water pressure at the bottom of the trench?
hint: The crushing pressure is extreme down there.

questionText: What do we call organisms that produce their own light?
hint: Deep-sea life uses bioluminescence.

questionText: Which deep-sea fish attracts prey with a glowing lure?
hint: The anglerfish dangles a glowing lure.

questionText: Where is the hadal zone found?
hint: Hadal zones are the very deepest parts of the sea.

questionText: What heats the water around deep-sea vents?
hint: Hydrothermal vents release superheated water.

questionText: What do bacteria near hydrothermal vents use for energy?
hint: Vent bacteria live by chemosynthesis.

questionText: How long ago did dinosaurs first appear?
hint: Dinosaurs ruled for over 150 million years.

questionText: What do we call the remains of ancient life preserved in rock?
hint: Fossils can be bones, teeth, or footprints.

questionText: Which dinosaur had three horns on its head?
hint: Its name means three-horned face.

questionText: Which dinosaur is known for the plates on its back?
hint: The plates run down its back to its tail.

questionText: What did plant-eating dinosaurs eat?
hint: Plant-eaters are called herbivores.

questionText: What did meat-eating dinosaurs eat?
hint: Meat-eaters are called carnivores.

questionText: Did all dinosaurs live in the sea?
hint: Dinosaurs were land animals.

questionText: What came out of dinosaur eggs?
hint: All dinosaurs hatched from eggs.

questionText: Which dinosaur name means king tyrant lizard?
hint: T. rex was one of the biggest meat-eaters.

questionText: Were all dinosaurs enormous giants?
hint: Some were no bigger than a chicken.

questionText: Which flying reptile lived at the same time as dinosaurs?
hint: Pterodactyls flew on wings of skin.

questionText: What is the study of prehistoric life called?
hint: Paleontologists dig up fossils.

questionText: How do scientists learn what dinosaurs ate?
hint: Sharp teeth mean meat-eaters.

questionText: Which small dinosaur was a fast hunter?
hint: It ran on two legs and had big claws.

questionText: Which dinosaur had a heavy club on its tail?
hint: The club could smash attackers.

questionText: What were the biggest dinosaurs called?
hint: Sauropods had long necks and giant bodies.

questionText: Where have most dinosaur fossils been found?
hint: Fossils appear on every continent.

questionText: Which dinosaur had a big bony frill around its neck?
hint: The frill helped protect its neck.

questionText: Did many dinosaurs build nests for their eggs?
hint: Fossil nests have been found with eggs.

questionText: What color were dinosaurs?
optionC: We do not know for sure
hint: Skin rarely survives as a fossil.

questionText: Which animals alive today are the closest relatives of dinosaurs?
hint: Birds evolved from small dinosaurs.

questionText: How did most dinosaurs move?
hint: Most walked or ran on legs.

questionText: What did the smallest dinosaurs often eat?
hint: Small jaws ate small food.

questionText: What is a full set of fossil bones called?
hint: Skeletons show how an animal stood.

questionText: Which dinosaur used sharp spikes on its tail for defense?
hint: Its tail spikes pointed outward.

questionText: Did humans ever live at the same time as dinosaurs?
hint: Dinosaurs died out 66 million years ago.

questionText: What do scientists use to tell the age of dinosaur fossils?
hint: Deeper rocks are usually older.

questionText: Which word means an animal that eats meat?
hint: Carnivores hunt other animals.

questionText: Which dinosaur had a giant sail on its back?
hint: The sail may have kept it warm or cool.

questionText: What evidence shows that some dinosaurs lived in herds?
hint: Many footprints in the same line suggest a herd.

questionText: Why did T. rex have such short arms?
optionA: No one knows for sure, many ideas exist
hint: Scientists debate the arms' use.

questionText: What are coprolites?
hint: They can show what an animal ate.

questionText: Which dinosaur had a dome of thick bone on its skull?
hint: It may have butted rivals with its dome.

questionText: What may Stegosaurus plates have been used for?
optionB: To control heat or show off
hint: They were too thin for armor.

questionText: Which ocean reptiles lived alongside dinosaurs?
hint: They swam in ancient seas.

questionText: What do growth rings in dinosaur bones tell us?
hint: Rings build up each year, like a tree's.

questionText: Which dinosaur could have up to 500 teeth?
hint: It kept growing new teeth all its life.

questionText: What is a dinosaur trackway?
hint: Trackways record a dinosaur's walk.

questionText: Which famous fossil site is in Utah, USA?
hint: It holds many Allosaurus bones.

questionText: What did the hollow crest of Parasaurolophus likely do?
hint: Air flowed through it to make calls.

questionText: Were dinosaurs warm-blooded?
hint: Bones and growth hint at both ideas.

questionText: Which dinosaurs often had feathers?
hint: Fossils show feather impressions.

questionText: What protected Ankylosaurus?
optionB: Bony armor and a tail club
hint: It was built like a living tank.

questionText: Which horned dinosaurs may have lived in herds?
hint: Bonebeds suggest they traveled in groups.

questionText: What do we call a baby dinosaur that just hatched?
hint: Hatchlings grew fast in the wild.

questionText: On which supercontinent did dinosaurs first appear?
hint: All the land was joined together then.

questionText: What is the most accepted cause of the dinosaurs' extinction?
hint: A huge crater supports this idea.

questionText: Where did the giant impact crater strike?
hint: The Chicxulub crater is there.

questionText: What is the impact crater called?
hint: It is hidden below rock and water.

questionText: Which element found in rock layers is a clue to the impact?
hint: Iridium is rare on Earth but common in asteroids.

questionText: Which era came after the dinosaurs died out?
hint: Mammals rose to power in this era.

questionText: Which ancient reptiles could truly fly?
hint: Their wings were made of skin.

questionText: What is a pterodactyl's wing made of?
optionC: A membrane of skin and muscle
hint: The wing stretched from body to finger.

questionText: Which bird-like dinosaurs have been found fossilized in China?
hint: China's rocks preserve feathered dinosaurs.

questionText: What is the name of the wall that surrounds a castle?
hint: It wrapped around the whole castle.

questionText: What was the main entrance to a castle called?
hint: Guards watched the gate night and day.

questionText: What heavy gate did castles lower to block entry?
hint: It was a heavy iron-tipped grill.

questionText: Who lived inside a medieval castle?
hint: Castles were homes for the rich.

questionText: What is a tall, narrow castle window called?
hint: Archers fired arrows through it.

questionText: What did guards walk along at the top of castle walls?
hint: Battlements had gaps for shooting.

questionText: What is the strongest stone tower in a castle called?
hint: The keep was the last safe place.

questionText: What body of water often surrounded a castle for defense?
hint: A moat could be filled with water.

questionText: What bridge could be raised to block a castle gate?
hint: It was lowered only for friends.

questionText: Which room stored a castle's food?
hint: Pantries kept grain and dried meats.

questionText: Where did knights keep their horses?
hint: Stables held horses and supplies.

questionText: What did knights wear to protect their heads?
hint: Helmets were made of metal.

questionText: Which weapon did knights use while riding horses?
hint: A lance was a long spear.

questionText: What did a king wear on his head?
hint: Crowns showed royal power.

questionText: Who worked in the fields for the lord?
hint: Most people were peasants.

questionText: Where did medieval towns hold their markets?
hint: Traders set up stalls there.

questionText: Which building stood at the center of village life?
hint: People gathered there on Sundays.

questionText: What did knights hold to block swords and arrows?
hint: Shields were often painted with signs.

questionText: What was the big meeting and feasting room in a castle?
hint: Feasts and courts happened there.

questionText: Who advised the king on important matters?
hint: Nobles were powerful lords.

questionText: What did a castle bell often warn people of?
hint: Bells signaled alarms and times.

questionText: Which metals were used to make a knight's armor?
hint: Iron and steel were strong and tough.

questionText: What did loyal knights receive from their king?
hint: Land brought wealth and power.

questionText: What is a medieval singer of tales called?
hint: Minstrels traveled and sang for lords.

questionText: What was the open courtyard inside castle walls called?
hint: People stored carts and animals there.

questionText: What did peasants grow in their fields?
hint: Crops fed the whole manor.

questionText: Which craft used hot ovens to make bread?
hint: Bakers worked in the town.

questionText: What did knights do at tournaments?
hint: Knights fought with lances on horseback.

questionText: What was the code of honor for knights called?
hint: It meant courage, loyalty, and courtesy.

questionText: What did a knight promise to give his lord?
hint: Loyalty held the whole system together.

questionText: Which weapon was a heavy ball swung on a chain?
hint: A flail could smash through armor.

questionText: What did a squire do for a knight?
hint: A squire learned to fight and care for armor.

questionText: Which knight served the legendary King Arthur?
hint: Lancelot was a famous knight of the Round Table.

questionText: What was a knight's war horse called?
hint: Destriers were strong and fast.

questionText: What did a gauntlet protect?
hint: Gauntlets were the gloves of armor.

questionText: What is the hilt of a sword?
hint: The knight gripped the hilt.

questionText: Who trained a young page for knighthood?
hint: Pages learned manners and skills at court.

questionText: Which armor was made from linked metal rings?
hint: Rings let the wearer move freely.

questionText: What did a knight carry to show his family identity?
hint: Coats of arms decorated shields and banners.

questionText: Which weapon shot arrows?
hint: Longbows could shoot very far.

questionText: What protected a knight's chest?
hint: The breastplate covered the torso.

questionText: Who were serfs in medieval society?
hint: Serfs worked the lord's land.

questionText: What was the medieval social system of land for loyalty called?
hint: Lords gave land for service.

questionText: Which legendary outlaw stole from the rich?
hint: He shared with the poor in Sherwood Forest.

questionText: What marked the end of a young man's training?
hint: A ceremony made him a knight.

questionText: What was a castle dungeon used for?
hint: Dungeons were dark prison rooms.

questionText: What shaped the daily life of medieval peasants most?
hint: Crops were planted and harvested by season.

questionText: Which terrible plague swept across medieval Europe?
hint: It killed millions in the 1300s.

questionText: What did lords give to peasants in exchange for their work?
hint: Peasants farmed in return for safety.

questionText: Who were the fierce raiders from Scandinavia?
hint: Vikings sailed in long ships.

questionText: What did guilds do in medieval towns?
hint: Guilds set standards for craft work.

questionText: Which metals were used to make medieval coins?
hint: Precious metals backed the money.

questionText: Which battle ended the Wars of the Roses?
hint: It put Henry Tudor on the throne.

questionText: What else was the great hall used for besides feasts?
hint: Lords held court and judged disputes there.

questionText: What is the bottom layer of the rainforest called?
hint: It is dark and covered with leaves.

questionText: Which animals are found in the rainforest canopy?
hint: Canopy dwellers are expert climbers.

questionText: What do rainforest plants need most?
hint: The rainforest is warm and wet.

questionText: What color are most tree frogs?
hint: Green helps them hide in leaves.

questionText: Which big cat lives in the rainforest?
hint: Jaguars are strong, spotted hunters.

questionText: What do rainforest trees give us?
hint: Trees make oxygen for us to breathe.

questionText: Which bird can learn to repeat words?
hint: Parrots are clever talkers.

questionText: What is the very top layer of tall trees called?
hint: The tallest trees rise above the rest.

questionText: Which ant builds large nests high in trees?
hint: They sew leaves together with silk.

questionText: What do sloths do for most of the day?
hint: Sloths can sleep up to 20 hours.

questionText: Which fruit grows on rainforest trees?
hint: Bananas grow in the tropics.

questionText: What is the middle layer of the rainforest called?
hint: It sits below the canopy.

questionText: Which reptile hangs from trees?
hint: Tree snakes glide through the branches.

questionText: Why is the rainforest so green?
optionA: Because there are so many plants
hint: Thousands of plant species grow there.

questionText: Which animal has a mask of dark fur around its eyes?
hint: The dark mask is its most famous feature.

questionText: Which bird has a huge colorful beak?
hint: Its beak is big but very light.

questionText: Which is the world's smallest monkey?
hint: It can sit in the palm of your hand.

questionText: Why is the rainforest so wet?
hint: It can rain for hours every day.

questionText: Which butterfly has brilliant blue wings?
hint: Its blue shimmer is famous.

questionText: What do many rainforest frogs lay in the water?
hint: Frog eggs hatch into tadpoles.

questionText: Which plant climbs up tree trunks?
hint: Vines reach the light high above.

questionText: Which big colorful bird lives in the Amazon?
hint: Macaws have bright red and blue feathers.

questionText: What do toucans use their big beaks to reach?
hint: The beak reaches food at the branch tips.

questionText: Which monkey swings by its tail?
hint: Its tail works like a fifth hand.

questionText: What color is the leaf of most trees?
hint: Chlorophyll makes leaves green.

questionText: Which small wild cat leaps between tree branches?
hint: Margays can jump from branch to branch.

questionText: Which creature spins webs between trees?
hint: Spiders spin silky webs to catch prey.

questionText: Which bird drums on tree trunks for insects?
hint: Its beak taps bark to find bugs.

questionText: Which ape builds a new nest high in trees each night?
hint: Orangutans sleep in leafy nests.

questionText: Which huge snake squeezes its prey?
hint: Anacondas coil around their prey.

questionText: What do leaf-cutter ants grow from the leaves they collect?
hint: They farm fungus for food.

questionText: Which frog is brightly colored and poisonous?
hint: Its bright colors warn hunters.

questionText: Which flying mammal lives in rainforest caves?
hint: Bats fly out to hunt at night.

questionText: Which great ape lives in African forests?
hint: Gorillas are strong plant-eaters.

questionText: What do canopy plants get from growing high up?
hint: Light is easiest to reach up high.

questionText: Which eagle hunts monkeys from the canopy?
hint: The harpy eagle is huge and powerful.

questionText: Which insect looks exactly like a leaf?
hint: It hides from hunters by disguise.

questionText: Which rodent is the world's largest?
hint: Capybaras can weigh over 50 kilograms.

questionText: Which flowers grow on rainforest trees?
hint: Many orchids bloom high in the canopy.

questionText: Which crocodilian lurks in Amazon rivers?
hint: Caimans are close cousins of alligators.

questionText: Which snake is one of the deadliest pit vipers in the rainforest?
hint: Its venom is very powerful.

questionText: Which fish builds nests and guards its eggs?
hint: Parent fish watch over the young.

questionText: What do sloths mostly eat?
hint: Leaves are slow to digest, so sloths rest a lot.

questionText: Which big bird has a helmet-like casque on its head?
hint: The casque sits on top of its beak.

questionText: Which insects build giant mound colonies?
hint: Termite mounds can be taller than a person.

questionText: Which colorful lizard climbs on trees?
hint: Anoles can change their color.

questionText: What is the first priority if you get lost in a jungle?
hint: You can survive days without food but not water.

questionText: What makes a good jungle shelter?
hint: Natural materials keep off the rain.

questionText: How can you signal for help from the air?
optionB: Build a campfire on the beach only
hint: Big letters and bright colors catch the eye.

questionText: Which sound carries farthest in a jungle?
hint: Whistles are loud and sharp.

questionText: How can you use a watch to find north?
optionA: Point the hour hand at the sun
hint: Halfway between the hour hand and 12 is south.

questionText: Which is a sign that water is safe to drink?
hint: Moving water is usually cleaner.

questionText: When is the best time to travel in the hot jungle?
hint: The cool hours save your energy.

questionText: What should you do if you meet a wild animal?
hint: Moving slowly is less threatening.
